original_test_intent: Verify the exact BMC OEM GPU interface provides mutually consistent, correct Sensor, Power, FirmwareVersion, EventLog/Entries and UpdateStatus data for the intended GPU inventory.
original_method: Using the vendor API schema and immutable BMC-to-GPU mapping, discover the Manager/OEM resource, issue bounded secure GETs for all five source endpoints in one observation window, normalize units/status/timestamps, redact event data and compare cross-endpoint identity/state to the project baseline.
manual_activity: The owner/vendor supplies OEM schema, GPU identity and expected units/version/event/update contract, approves sensitive event retention and adjudicates semantic correctness.
required_inputs: Vendor OEM API/spec revision and exact endpoint/resource schemas
BMC/Manager/firmware identity and OEM GPU IDs to physical GPU/OAM/serial mapping
Expected sensor names/units/ranges/statuses and power aggregation/limits
Expected firmware components/versions and UpdateStatus state meanings
EventLog pagination/size/time window plus sensitive-data redaction/retention policy
TLS trust and protected read-only credential
safety_requirements: Verify vendor path and physical GPU identity before interpreting values
Use certificate validation/protected secrets; no -k or root password on command line
GET only; prohibit OEM update/reset/clear-event/action requests
Bound EventLog pagination/size/time and redact security/topology/fault details
Stop on active/ambiguous update, cross-endpoint GPU mismatch, inconsistent timestamps, schema/unit ambiguity or unsafe output
agent_execution_scope: Discover/verify exact OEM GPU resource, schemas and physical mapping
GET Sensor, Power, FirmwareVersion, EventLog/Entries and UpdateStatus exactly once per approved bounded snapshot
Validate status/schema/units/count/pagination and correlate identity/timestamps across endpoints
Apply redaction and compare fields to the vendor/owner baseline
Perform no update, reset, clear or independent health verdict
engineer_actions: Provide vendor API, GPU mapping and expected sensor/power/firmware/event/update matrix
Approve event-data policy and handling of in-progress/stale UpdateStatus
Review all-five-endpoint correlation and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Sensor/Power/FirmwareVersion GETs are relevant but incomplete because source explicitly includes EventLog/Entries and UpdateStatus. All sample commands also use insecure TLS/CLI secrets and lack vendor schema, identity and bounds.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a verified vendor-compatible Redfish client to securely fetch all five resources under one bounded snapshot, validate OEM schemas/units/identity and redact events before cross-endpoint comparison.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Exact five endpoint names, response-correctness objective and 5/5-minute estimates remain; no endpoint may be omitted because another reports generic GPU health.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Generate a correlation manifest keyed by physical GPU and OEM resource ID, with each endpoint's timestamp/hash/schema version; normalize sensor/power units, component versions, event window and update state before evaluating consistency.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds secure vendor-aware identity, complete endpoint coverage, bounds/redaction and cross-endpoint causality rather than independent insecure JSON reads.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Three endpoints cannot infer event history or update state; likewise a healthy Sensor response cannot prove firmware/version or power correctness. All five are independent source coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OEM semantics may change by firmware, event collections may be large/sensitive and UpdateStatus can be transient. Values cannot be judged without the vendor contract and synchronized snapshot.

project_override_considerations: If an endpoint is deprecated or renamed, the approved vendor mapping must name its replacement and demonstrate equivalent fields; it cannot simply reduce the five-endpoint denominator.
expected_evidence: Exact source row/variant/hash, vendor spec and BMC/Manager/OEM/physical-GPU identities
Redacted hashed Sensor and Power JSON with units/status/range comparisons
FirmwareVersion component matrix and expected-version comparison
UpdateStatus state/timestamp plus cross-endpoint identity/time consistency
No-action audit, discrepancies and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure consistently requires five OEM GPU read endpoints and Criteria applies to their data. DeepSeek's omission is a prior-review coverage defect, not an ambiguity in the authoritative source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Vendor specification, mapping and expected values gate execution but do not prevent complete static review; absent package is tracked without claiming hardware failure.

review_improvement: Restores omitted event/update coverage and makes five OEM resources a single identity-correlated, vendor-schema-validated and privacy-bounded snapshot.
independent_technical_reasoning: The five resources answer different questions: instantaneous sensor health, power telemetry, installed firmware identity, historical events and update lifecycle. None is a safe proxy for another. Their GPU identifiers and timestamps must agree because otherwise values may come from different devices or update epochs. UpdateStatus is especially important when firmware readings/events are changing; an active update invalidates a nominally static comparison and requires an explicit stop rather than polling or invoking an action.
